candidates.title: Directed codebook geometry with a non-collapse margin
candidates.falsifier: On the checker, exchanging source and target must change the loss and all declared gradients must be finite. After the single cold run, a nonzero codebook update with no improvement in the frozen Stage-3 recall@10 and NDCG@10 versus control falsifies the proposed useful-geometry mechanism; a decrease in transition-pair codeword separation or severe occupancy collapse falsifies its non-convergence rationale.
candidates.risk: The midpoint-distance ordering may be poorly aligned with recommendation utility, and fixed hard assignments make the signal piecewise and sparse. The codebook may satisfy the margin by moving codewords in a way that harms other items or creates unstable assignment boundaries; the small weight limits but does not eliminate that risk.
candidates.codebook_interaction: For each valid pair, the loss compares the midpoint's distances to the two endpoint-assigned codewords and pushes their distance difference toward the positive margin. The endpoint assignments are hard indices and are held fixed for differentiation. This does not minimize the distance between the two codewords: the codebook gradient acts through their distinct distances to the midpoint, while delta requires a nonzero distance difference rather than convergence. If the margin is already met, the pair contributes only a small softplus tail.

candidates.title: Directed assignment-structure balancing with endpoint separation
candidates.falsifier: The checker must observe finite nonzero codebook gradients, zero source/target gradients, and a loss change when source and target are exchanged. The proposal is falsified if a cold run shows reduced transition-pair separation or a collapsed occupancy pattern, or if Stage-3 recall@10 and NDCG@10 fail to improve over the archived control.
candidates.risk: The separation penalty may repeatedly push apart frequently co-occurring codewords without improving useful item neighborhoods, and the hard usage-balance term is nondifferentiable with respect to codebook positions in this specified implementation. If few transitions fall below rho, the only gradient-bearing component may be sparse; if many do, it may distort the codebook globally.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The separation term directly differentiates the distance between the two endpoint-assigned codewords and penalizes only distances below rho, pushing those codewords apart rather than together. The usage term is computed from hard source assignments held fixed for differentiation, so it has no gradient through the discrete counts; it affects the objective value but contributes no codebook force under this definition. Thus the guaranteed nonzero codebook path is the separation term, and it cannot pull a transition's two codewords together.

candidates.title: Directed behavior-conditioned residual transport to separated code anchors
candidates.falsifier: The checker must confirm that swapping source and target changes the loss and that all declared gradients are finite and nonzero. In the cold run, a fall in median transition-pair codeword separation, widespread pair distances below rho, or no improvement in frozen Stage-3 recall@10 and NDCG@10 versus control falsifies the mechanism or its anti-collapse safeguard.
candidates.risk: Identity residual transport may be an incorrect model of behavior-conditioned dynamics, and its codebook gradients may still indirectly bring endpoint codewords together while fitting the residual relation. The separation safeguard only prevents that locally for pairs below rho and may trade off transport fit against codebook geometry. The small transport weight reduces but cannot remove the risk of harming downstream neighborhoods.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The transport residual differentiates into both assigned codewords, with the source codeword entering through the source residual and the target codeword through the target residual. The additional hinge-like softplus safeguard differentiates the endpoint codeword distance only when it is below rho and pushes the pair apart. The transport term alone has no guarantee against convergence, so the explicit separation safeguard is essential; its weight and threshold must be checked against actual pair-distance measurements.
